title: Java RCE — ObjectInputStream.readObject on an attacker-supplied request body
note: The cast to SessionState happens AFTER readObject has already constructed the graph, so it is not a control: gadget chains on the classpath execute during deserialization. P0, and the fix is not a try-with-resources tweak (which the code already has) but refusing Java-native deserialization of untrusted bytes, or an ObjectInputFilter allowlist. Impact wording matters as much as the rating: the PATH is confirmed, the RCE IMPACT is assessed until the classpath is inventoried (see AE-5). Remediation must also name the right filter API for the target's Java version — java.io.ObjectInputFilter is 9+; on 8 it is -Djdk.serialFilter (8u121+) or the internal sun.misc.ObjectInputFilter.
severity_note: P0, exactly — no band. The unverified condition here (the classpath gadget inventory) is an AGGRAVATING one, and SKILL.md § Evidence Confidence says an unverified aggravating condition moves the severity in neither direction. A band would have made the grader reward the downgrade the document forbids; that contradiction is what the first fix shipped. Conservatism about this condition belongs in `impact_basis`, graded below. A band is legitimate only where the uncertainty is about REACHABILITY or an upstream control, and such a fixture must also declare `severity_deviation_condition`.

impact_depends_on_unverified.why: Arbitrary Serializable instantiation and unbounded graph expansion are established from the code alone; remote code execution additionally needs a gadget chain reachable on this classpath, which a static review cannot see.
